competitorWins: GDELT is genuinely stronger as a raw global knowledge resource: the largest open spatio-temporal dataset ever created, monitoring news in 100+ languages every 15 minutes with tone/sentiment, themes, people, and organization coding — queryable at limitless scale via BigQuery, with archives back to 1979. For data scientists and researchers doing global-scale analysis, nothing free comes close. Note that WorldEye's own Pro intel feeds build on GDELT — they are complementary, not substitutes.
description: GDELT (Global Database of Events, Language, and Tone) monitors broadcast, print, and web news from nearly every country in 100+ languages, updating every 15 minutes. The entire database is 100% free and open: raw CSV bulk downloads, a free Analysis Service for visualization, a DOC 2.0 full-text API, and the full event database in Google BigQuery. It differs from WorldEye by being a raw machine-coded global event database for analysts and developers — no 3D globe, cameras, flight/ship tracking, or ready-made consumer map — while WorldEye turns GDELT-style feeds into a free no-signup live globe with paid Pro tools on top.
